nodes.check: the harness emits at least one challenger design, and G5 accepts it
nodes.sabotage: strip design_source from the emitted challenger -> the check goes red
nodes.brief_given: the challenge, the corpus harness, and TASK_TYPES' challenger rule
nodes.intent: make the corpus harness emit a challenger arm so G5 can execute

stop.criteria: a challenger design appears in the emitted corpus and passes the gate
stop.baseline: everything the baseline recorded as passing still passes
stop.must_not_change: the 300 default designs and their labels

nodes.returns: the edited harness and the emitted challenger proofs

loop.exit: a fresh node on the stronger tier with the check's output

nodes.check: a test validates a challenger ledger row, and fails if G5 or G7 is removed
nodes.sabotage: delete the G5 clause -> the new test goes red
nodes.brief_given: the challenge, the emitted challenger, and the ledger template
nodes.intent: pin G5 and G7 with a test that fails when either rule is removed

stop.criteria: both rules have a test that goes red when the rule is deleted
stop.baseline: everything the baseline recorded as passing still passes
stop.must_not_change: the existing test suite's other assertions

nodes.returns: the test file and the proof it fails without the rule

loop.exit: a fresh node on the stronger tier with the check's output

nodes.check: fixed checklist: the diff is read against the challenge, findings cite file:line
nodes.brief_given: the diff and the challenge, never the builders' reasoning
nodes.intent: an independent read of what changed

stop.criteria: every checklist item answered with a finding or a clean pass
stop.baseline: everything the baseline recorded as passing still passes
stop.must_not_change: nothing; this node reviews and does not edit

nodes.returns: findings with file:line, or an explicit clean pass

estimate.basis: two small edits in one test harness, plus a review
